openings.claim: Does A1's movement-linked upkeep fit the ten-minute daily preparation limit when qualifying work after opening is included?
openings.delta: Test the accounting dependency behind the claimed fit; separating post-opening upkeep does not establish compliance.
openings.prediction: If post-opening corrections are necessary preparation, total qualifying work can exceed ten minutes even when pre-opening preparation stops at ten.
openings.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative is that post-opening upkeep is ordinary handoff service and adds no preparation; total preparation remains within ten minutes, although service burden may persist.
openings.defeat: A complete daily work trace shows all qualifying preparation, including corrections, totals at most ten minutes without deferred necessary work.
openings.probe: Propose a sole-clerk, private timing-sheet audit of existing preparation and corrections, classifying their purpose and summing qualifying minutes across the day. Cap any added audit preparation within the remaining ten-minute allowance; do not introduce movement updates.
assumptions: Fit concerns the capped audit, not A1's sustained intervention.
Synthetic stipulations establish neither observed benefit nor a settled classification of upkeep.

openings.claim: Can Z1's assumed existing private evidence reliably distinguish the reserving reader from another household member?
openings.delta: Expose the identity-verification dependency: current physical location alone cannot establish the correct recipient.
openings.prediction: If private reservation identity cannot be distinguished, accurate locators still leave household ownership ambiguous and correct handoffs unproven.
openings.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative is a storage-indexing error only: existing private evidence already identifies the reserving reader reliably despite household surname placement.
openings.defeat: Existing private evidence consistently resolves the reservation owner independently of the shelf surname in the relevant household cases.
openings.probe: Propose a bounded sole-clerk review of whatever existing private reservation evidence is available for household cases, without changing storage or handoff rules. Keep names behind the desk and all added preparation within ten daily minutes; missing evidence leaves the question unresolved.
assumptions: Availability and adequacy of private reservation evidence are unconfirmed.
Fit evaluates the proposed review; reliable identity checks and intervention benefits remain unproven.

critiques.issue: Separate post-opening accounting leaves C4 compliance unresolved.
Linking locators to reservation identity depends on unverified private evidence.
